During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, cash outflow from accounts receivable was $2.2 million, as compared to cash inflow of $29.1 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease in cash flow from accounts receivable for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the prior year period was primarily due to growth in revenue at existing units and the impact of acquisitions, partially offset by a decrease in days sales outstanding (“DSO”).

DSO is one of the key factors that we use to evaluate the condition of our accounts receivable and the related allowances for contractual adjustments and uncollectibles. DSO reflects the timeliness of cash collections on billed revenue and the level of reserves on outstanding accounts receivable. Our DSO was 42.5 days at September 30, 2026 as compared to 42.8 days at December 31, 2025 and 43.1 days at September 30, 2025.

da.text: Depreciation and amortization expense was $6.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $5.6 million for the same period in 2025. The net increase of $0.7 million was primarily related to capital expenditures at our existing units and from capital expenditures and amortization of intangible assets from recent acquisitions.

intro.text: Pediatrix is a leading provider of physician services including newborn, maternal-fetal, and other pediatric subspecialty care. Our national network is comprised of affiliated physicians who provide clinical care in 37 states. During 2024, we formalized our practice portfolio management plans, resulting in a decision to exit almost all of our affiliated office-based practices, other than maternal-fetal medicine. As of December 31, 2024, these plans were completed. Additionally, we exited our primary and urgent care service line during 2024 based on a review of the cost and time that would be required to build the platform to scale.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Administrative fees accounted for approximately 14% of our net revenue for 2025.
During 2025, approximately 64% of our net revenue was generated by operations in our five largest states.
Our operations in Texas accounted for approximately 32% of our net revenue for the same period.
In particular, Texas accounted for approximately 32% of our net revenue in 2025.
During 2025 and 2024, approximately 64% and 67%, respectively, of our net revenue was generated by operations in our five largest states.
During both 2025 and 2024, our operations in Texas accounted for approximately 32% of our net revenue.
For example, the gross amount billed to patients covered under GHC Programs for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 represented approximately 53% of our total gross patient service revenue.
The decrease in revenue of $99.1 million, or 4.9%, was primarily attributable to non-same unit revenue, primarily from practice dispositions, partially offset by an increase in same-unit revenue.

The ultimate impact of any tariffs will depend on various factors, including if any tariffs are ultimately implemented, the timing of implementation, and the amount, scope and nature of the tariffs.
Our ability to make payments on and to refinance our debt will depend on our ability to generate cash in the future.
Our ability to restructure or refinance our debt will depend on the condition of the capital markets and our financial condition at such time.

We rely on a multidisciplinary team, including our information security organization, legal department, management, and third-party service providers , as described further below, to assess, identify, and manage cybersecurity threats and risks.
The amount and timing of repurchases will depend upon several factors, including general economic and market conditions and trading restrictions.
We encourage investors to review our financial statements and publicly-filed reports in their entirety and not to rely on any single financial measure.

The Company has not included an accrual for these matters as of December 31, 2025 in its Consolidated Financial Statements, as the variables affecting any potential eventual liability depend on the currently unknown facts and circumstances that arise out of, and are specific to, any particular future audit, inquiry and investigation and cannot be reasonably estimated at this time.
